question: Could any material object be perceived if creation were not consciousness-made?
premises: Suppose this creation were merely material and not made of consciousness.
Perception would then have to arise from within that material creation.
No one could perceive even a single mountain from within such a merely material creation.
inference: Because perception occurs, creation cannot be merely material; it must be consciousness-made.
plain_english: If this creation were merely material and not made of consciousness, then no one could perceive even a single mountain from within it.
